title: Lease presence core
description: Objective: implement fenced assignment, workspace, resource, and provider-slot lease state plus separate non-authoritative presence. Deliverable: scheduler authority modules with epoch, renew, suspect, drain, revoke, and race property tests. NOT in scope: provider launch, OS locks, policy decisions, or graph fan-out. Hard dependencies: Runtime contract registry and Identity session core. Owned paths: packages/scheduler/src/authority/**. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler test.
definitionOfDone: Every authority mutation requires the current token and epoch; stale renew/release/complete has zero business effect.
Presence cannot create, renew, steal, or release a lease.
Suspect, drain, revoke, handoff, and restart races end in one legal deterministic state.
The focused scheduler typecheck and test command exits 0.
taskRails: Follow the pinned design; this task cannot create authority beyond its named contract.
Fail closed with stable codes and immutable deterministic outputs.
Keep production modules focused, target <=250 lines, split before 400.
Use TDD and stage only explicit owned paths; no worktree, broad add, push, or merge.

implementationPlan.description: TDD red — src/authority/lease-state.test.ts. FENCING MATRIX (DoD 1) — all seven design-749 checks that are shape-expressible: {wrong leaseToken, stale epoch, wrong authorityHashRef, stale record version, wrong lease state, present-but-MISMATCHED ownerSessionRef} × every mutation -> ZERO business effect + an atomic REDACTED rejection-security record; REDACTION IS PRECISE: leaseToken ABSENT from the record, expectedEpoch/observedEpoch PRESENT (registry EPOCHS detail keys are the required safe scalars — blanket redaction would make the record unmappable); MISSING/shape-invalid ownerSessionRef is NOT a security event — design 749 reserves the security record for authenticated, syntactically valid attempts — it yields plain AUTHORITY_MALFORMED_INPUT with no security record (assert absence). Capability check is documented out of scope (dependency-free reducer). STATE MACHINE (design 12.2): ACTIVE->SUSPECT->ACTIVE, ACTIVE|SUSPECT->DRAINING->RELEASED|REVOKED, ACTIVE|SUSPECT|DRAINING->REVOKED (privileged, carries reason); fencedRenew accepts ACTIVE|SUSPECT with valid token/epoch and restores ACTIVE (SUSPECT->ACTIVE is the owner's renew path — the wrong-state set for renew is exactly DRAINING/RELEASED/REVOKED); extend is the human-side recovery carrying a reason; markSuspect is a due-observation EVENT record (timer has NO authority); epoch increments ONLY on successor/revocation; renewal stores server wall deadline + boot ID + monotonic observation; frozen constants RENEWAL_WINDOW_SECONDS=90 and RENEW_AFTER_SECONDS=30 (integer arithmetic, no 1/3 float) with design citations, INSIDE lease-state.ts (no authority-policy.ts — no override surface exists; authority-policy.ts is the amendment split point if the module nears 400). RELEASE/HANDOFF (12.4, all THREE branches): (1) safe-boundary + all effects/resources terminal -> RELEASED atomically with bounded truth-classed handoff {completedSteps, activeProcessResourceFacts, inputDigest, worktreeDigest, contextDigest, journalDigest, artifactDigest (five families named explicitly), nextSafeAction}; (2) otherwise -> DRAINING + cancellation/reconciliation intent refs + releasePending: true (NEVER 'released'); (3) handoff FAILS bounded/truth-class validation -> authority REMAINS unchanged or becomes SUSPECT, NO partial handoff stored, NO DRAINING transition; later STRONGER drain reason (rank vocabulary) marks the tentative handoff non-resumable; DrainDisposition stores the COMPLETE reason set + monotonic strongest (union semantics: no request removes a reason, only higher rank changes target, equal-rank ties by stable reason code); terminal/already-unassigned releases are idempotent no-ops that never resurrect terminal work; successor-claim logic is EXPLICITLY OUT (work.claim territory — this module's interface is the resumable/non-resumable flag). PROVIDER_SLOT is NOT in the lease kind union (design 741 scopes the 5-state machine to assignment/workspace leases; slots have a distinct RESERVED|ACTIVE lifecycle) — kind: ASSIGNMENT|WORKSPACE|RESOURCE only. Confirm RED.

TWO REAL DEFECTS THE RED TESTS CAUGHT AND I FIXED (not test edits to fit the code):
1. `isOverdue` originally treated a boot-id change as making a lease due. That would have marked EVERY ACTIVE lease SUSPECT on every daemon restart — a destructive false-positive. Dueness is now a server-wall fact only (`clock.serverWallSeconds > lease.serverWallDeadline`); the stored bootId scopes the monotonic observation and nothing else. The restart test now asserts the safe behaviour: a lease with a future deadline is NOT overdue after a boot change, while the reconstruction still reports the new bootId.
2. My token-leak sweep initially asserted "no token on ANY release path", which failed on the accepted path. Correct reading of design 749: redaction scopes the rejection-security record and error paths; the accepted result IS the authoritative lease row and must carry its token or the lease is unusable. Test now sweeps four REJECTED paths for both the current and the attempted token, plus a positive assertion that the accepted path returns the record with its token.

DESIGN POINTS IMPLEMENTED: check order is exactly design 749 (token -> epoch -> authority hash -> session -> version -> state) with first-failure-decides so a rejection never reports two causes; successor-epoch revocation is discriminated as AUTHORITY_SUPERSEDED_AUTHORITY (proof.epoch < lease.epoch AND state REVOKED) rather than AUTHORITY_STALE_EPOCH; epoch moves only in confirmRevoke and by exactly +1; every accepted mutation advances `version` by exactly 1; renewal stores serverWallSeconds+90, bootId, and the monotonic observation; RENEW_AFTER_SECONDS is the integer literal 30 (no float divide); release branch 3 validates the handoff BEFORE composing any transition, so authority is left exactly as found with no partial record; DrainDisposition recomposes from the full reason union on every apply (set semantics, alphabetical stable order, higher rank wins, equal rank ties by reason code) and a forged disposition whose strongestReason/terminalTarget/resumable disagree with its own reason set is refused; resumable is `strongestReason === "WORK_RELEASE_OR_PAUSE"` per design 765. No Date.now, no Math.random, no cross-package import: all observations are caller-supplied and all results are deep-frozen. Parsed records are fresh copies, so no caller-owned object is ever frozen by us (mem:gotcha-pure-reducer-deep-freeze-aliasing).

implementationPlan.description: TDD red then green — src/authority/lease-resource.ts (+ shim). All-or-none acquisition (design 12.2 final para): reserveAll({declaredResources, capacitySnapshot}) either reserves capacity units for ALL declared non-provider resources in CANONICAL resource-ID order or reserves NONE and returns a durable ResourceWaitRequest — shape FROZEN NOW for M2's fair scheduler (fields: requestId, canonical resource-ID set, eligibilityEventSequenceRef, continuouslyEligibleSinceRef, callerObservation — priority/ticket/aging state deliberately ABSENT, M2 owns queue selection; blocked-head-cannot-block-unrelated is a queue-selection property, also M2); PENDING_ACQUIRE rows with epochs + idempotent effect-intent refs; adapterConfirm(epoch) required per external resource before ACTIVE; ANY failed/unknown acquisition -> confirmed ones fenced/released, whole set held (typed result); only after all ACTIVE may the caller record a provider-slot RESERVATION ref — slots use their own two-state RESERVED|ACTIVE vocabulary (design 421), never the lease 5-state machine, and slot activation (effect.activate) is OUT of scope; release uncertainty -> quarantined record; successor receives no capacity until a fenceability/reconciliation proof ref is present. Tests in lease-state.test.ts extension or focused block: canonical ordering, none-on-any-failure, epoch-confirm gating, partial-failure fencing, wait-request shape determinism, quarantine.

PLANNED DEVIATION FROM THE PLAN TEXT, with reason (flagged at step-1, now landed): the plan said slots use a "two-state RESERVED|ACTIVE vocabulary". Both the registry (`RUNTIME_LIFECYCLES.PROVIDER_SLOT`, runtime-vocabulary.ts:53) and design line 222 are THREE-state `RESERVED|ACTIVE|RELEASED`. Since step-7's vocabulary-drift red-team compares local strings to the registry by value, `SLOT_STATES` is the three-state registry-identical set. Only `RESERVED` is minted here; `effect.activate` and release stay out of scope. The test asserts SLOT_STATES equals ["RESERVED","ACTIVE","RELEASED"] and explicitly that it contains none of SUSPECT/DRAINING/REVOKED, which is the real point — slots never enter the lease five-state machine.

IMPLEMENTED (19 new tests): canonical resource-id ordering on both the reserved rows and the wait request; all-or-none — a single short resource, or a resource absent from the capacity snapshot, reserves NOTHING and returns the wait request (asserted by the absence of "PENDING_ACQUIRE" anywhere in the payload); ResourceWaitRequest shape frozen and asserted by exact object equality {requestId, resourceIds, eligibilityEventSequenceRef, continuouslyEligibleSinceRef, callerObservation} with priority/ticket/aging deliberately absent (M2 owns queue selection); wait-request determinism (same input twice deep-equal); duplicate resource ids, negative epoch, empty requestId, and null all refused; non-external resources go straight ACTIVE while external ones sit at PENDING_ACQUIRE; effect-intent refs are derived deterministically as `intent:<requestId>:<resourceId>` so a retry reuses the same intent; adapterConfirm is epoch-fenced (wrong epoch -> AUTHORITY_STALE_EPOCH with the row set untouched) and refuses unknown, non-external, and already-ACTIVE rows; adapterFail with FAILED releases the confirmed fenceable rows and holds the whole set; with UNKNOWN it QUARANTINES the uncertain row; a confirmed row whose adapter cannot fence stale use is QUARANTINED rather than assumed released (design's "safety over invented liveness"); adapterFail is epoch-fenced too; reserveProviderSlot yields {slotRef, requestId, state:"RESERVED"} only when every row is ACTIVE and otherwise refuses with the stale-lease family; successor capacity is granted freely when nothing is quarantined, REFUSED while a quarantined row has no proof reference, and clears quarantine to RELEASED only against an explicit reconciliation proof ref. All results deep-frozen; parsers build fresh copies so no caller-owned object is ever frozen.

presence.ts structurally cannot express authority: PresenceProjection is {sessionRef, lastSeen, lastPingId} with no epoch/version/token/state field, and a test asserts none of those strings appear in a serialized projection. lastSeen is max(lastSeen, serverReceivedAt) so a delayed ping never moves it backwards; a repeated pingId is coalesced to the identical projection even with a much later timestamp; a cross-session ping is refused with PRESENCE_SESSION_MISMATCH; 7 hostile shapes (including an extra `leaseToken` field and an extra `epoch` field) are refused. The 10s cadence and <=1s batch window are documented as DAEMON behaviour in a comment and are deliberately NOT kernel constants.

NON-VACUITY EVIDENCE (the numbers the plan asked for). The race harness runs 5 seeds x 240 steps over the full alphabet {fencedRenew, markSuspect, extend, confirmRevoke, releaseWork, restartReconstruct, applyDrainReason, reserveAll, adapterConfirm, adapterFail}, starting from a 5-member state pool built by asserted-good sequences (ACTIVE/SUSPECT/DRAINING/RELEASED/REVOKED, each member's state asserted), with 70/30 biased selection between the current valid proof and one of five tampers, and re-entry into the pool on terminal states. The test asserts the observed outcome-kind SET equals an exact expected list of 18 kinds. Measured counts across the seed set: ACCEPT:ACTIVE 90, ACCEPT:SUSPECT 11, ACCEPT:DRAINING 38, ACCEPT:RELEASED 37, ACCEPT:REVOKED 68, ACCEPT:NO_OP 16, ACCEPT:DRAIN:RELEASED 3, ACCEPT:DRAIN:REVOKED 130, ACCEPT:RESERVED 57, ACCEPT:WAITING 52, ACCEPT:RESOURCE_ACTIVE 20, ACCEPT:RESOURCE_HELD 36, RESTART:0 75, RESTART:1 48, AUTHORITY_STALE_LEASE 460, AUTHORITY_MALFORMED_INPUT 29, AUTHORITY_STALE_EPOCH 26, AUTHORITY_SUPERSEDED_AUTHORITY 4. Every AUTHORITY_* code and every one of the five lease states is genuinely reached — including the rarest branch (superseded authority, 4 hits), which is exactly the branch a uniform random walk would have missed.

PER-STEP INVARIANTS ASSERTED INSIDE THE HARNESS (so they hold on all 1200 steps, not just at the end): the input record is deep-equal-unchanged after every command (purity); the version delta is always 0 or exactly 1; the epoch delta is always 0 or exactly 1 and never negative; any state change implies version+1; any epoch+1 implies the new state is REVOKED. Determinism: the same seed replays to a bit-identical trace and a different seed does not.

ONE REAL FINDING the harness caught: my first per-step assertion demanded version+1 whenever the returned record object differed by identity, which failed on the idempotent NO_OP release (a fresh copy at the same version). The production behaviour was right — a terminal release must have zero business effect — so the assertion was tightened to the correct invariant (delta in {0,1}, and a state change implies 1) rather than loosened.

ALSO ADDED (kernel invariants file): a scan asserting no production module contains Date.now, Math.random, "process.", "@moe/", or globalThis; the exactly-one-successor-epoch property (two concurrent confirmRevoke attempts against the same record both compute the SAME successor epoch record.epoch+1, never +2, the input is untouched, and once either is committed the other is refused with AUTHORITY_SUPERSEDED_AUTHORITY); a deep-freeze-aliasing check (our frozen result never freezes the caller's record); drain monotonicity over 5 seeds x 40 random reasons asserting the strongest rank never decreases and every earlier reason survives, with an aggregate assertion that all 7 reasons were actually drawn; and the vocabulary-drift check comparing LEASE_STATES, DRAIN_REASONS, and the rank set to the registry/design values.

implementationPlan.note:
Adversarial self-review done, TWO REAL DEFECTS FOUND AND FIXED, then committed by explicit pathspec.

DEFECT 1 — SILENT LEASE BRICKING (integer ceiling). `isCount` accepted `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`. The reducer then emitted `version + 1`, `epoch + 1`, or `serverWallSeconds + 90`, none of which are safe integers, so the successor record failed the SAME parse on every later command. The lease would become permanently unmutable — it could not even be revoked — and the mutation that created it returned ok:true, so nothing looked wrong. Probed and confirmed: `Number.isSafeInteger(MAX_SAFE_INTEGER + 1) === false`. FIX uses two bounds, because one is not enough (any single ceiling just moves the brick one step later): a PARSE bound `MAX_AUTHORITY_COUNT = MAX_SAFE_INTEGER - 1e6` so a record at the ceiling stays readable and reconcilable, and a strict MUTATION bound in `fenceAuthority` (`version >= MAX` or `epoch >= MAX` refuses) so no successor is ever emitted above the ceiling. `parseClock` caps `serverWallSeconds` at `MAX - RENEWAL_WINDOW_SECONDS` so the derived deadline still parses. Exhaustion is a property of the RECORD, not the attempt, so it yields AUTHORITY_MALFORMED_INPUT with securityRecord null. Three regression tests: a record at MAX_SAFE_INTEGER in any of four counters is refused; a record at the ceiling refuses mutation with no security record; a record one below the ceiling accepts and its successor still parses (asserted through restartReconstruct, which is the read path).

DEFECT 2 — LATENT THROW IN A FAIL-CLOSED KERNEL. `composeDisposition` used `reduce(strongerOf)` with no initial value, which throws TypeError on an empty array. Unreachable from today's two callers, but a pure kernel that must always return a typed rejection had a crash path one careless caller away. Fixed to return null on empty, with every caller mapping that to a typed rejection.

RED-TEAM CHECKLIST (a)-(g), all executed:
(a) PRESENCE LAUNDERING — presence.ts's public surface is openPresence/acceptPing over {sessionRef, lastSeen, lastPingId}; no lease field is reachable and no lease type is imported. Its import list is asserted to be EXACTLY ["../runtime-shape.js"] (not merely "contains no lease import"), every lease module is asserted to have zero /presence/ specifier, and a third test asserts the scanned production-file list equals the exact expected set so a NEW module cannot slip past the ban. It even carries its own isRef/isInstant/exactRecord rather than importing the shared kernel.
(b) TOKEN LEAKAGE — grepped every `leaseToken` occurrence in production: three type-declaration lines, two key-list entries, two parse guards, and one comparison in fenceAuthority. The value is never written into any output. RejectionSecurityRecord has no token field by construction; rejection messages name the failed check, never the value; issues are sorted by JSON.stringify of {code, message} only. Tests sweep four rejected release paths for both the current and the attempted token.
(c) EPOCH LAUNDERING — two concurrent confirmRevoke calls against the same record both compute the SAME successor (epoch+1, never +2), the input is untouched, and once either is committed the other is refused with AUTHORITY_SUPERSEDED_AUTHORITY. confirmRevoke on an already-REVOKED lease is refused by the legal-state set with the current proof and by the epoch check with the old one. The race harness additionally asserts on all 1200 steps that the epoch delta is 0 or 1, never negative, and that epoch+1 implies the new state is REVOKED.
(d) DRAIN REGRESSION — strongest is recomputed from the full union on every apply, so no operation sequence can remove a reason or lower the rank; asserted over 5 seeds x 40 random reasons with an aggregate check that all 7 reasons were drawn. A forged disposition whose strongestReason is not in its own reason set is refused. Documented explicitly in the source that the guarantee is per-application and durability of the accumulated set belongs to the persisting transaction.
(e) HANDOFF BRANCH 3 — handoff validation runs BEFORE any transition is composed. Five invalid handoffs assert record deep-equal-unchanged (structuredClone before/after), no partial handoff in the payload, and no "DRAINING" string anywhere in the result; a SUSPECT lease stays SUSPECT.
(f) VOCABULARY DRIFT — LEASE_STATES, DRAIN_REASONS, the rank set, SLOT_STATES, and ACQUISITION_STATES are all compared by value to the registry/design sets, with an extra assertion that SLOT_STATES contains none of SUSPECT/DRAINING/REVOKED.
(g) NO SCRATCH FILES — the authority directory contains exactly the 21 committed files. The temporary tally probe used to extract the non-vacuity counts was applied by sed and restored in the same command; verified by git status showing no stray path.

SKILL CHECKLIST ITEMS NOT COVERED ABOVE: concurrency — the package is pure reducers with no shared mutable state and no IO, so there is no check-then-act to lock; the token/epoch/version fencing
